title: Canonical polynomial fibre stalk and its regularity
statement: For a scheme map f:X→T, an open U⊆X and a chart e:U→A^n_T whose projection is f|U, construct the base changed chart over each residue field and the open fibre inclusion [def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. At x∈U define R as the stalk of the polynomial fibre at the chart image and φ:R→S as its stalk map followed by the inverse open-immersion stalk isomorphism, where S is the actual f-fibre stalk. This is a local map, and R is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. If e is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], φ is quasi-finite.

source.place: Tags 00RH and 00RE: polynomial chart, fibre localization and regularity.

proof.text: Use pullback associativity to construct the open fibre inclusion and the base changed chart. Define the open fibre point with the fibre homeomorphism. The pullback equations show its image is f.asFiber(U.ι x). Define φ by the chart stalk map, the inverse inclusion stalk map, and transport along this point equality. Scheme stalk maps and isomorphisms are local. Base change and localization preserve quasi-finiteness; its composition with ring isomorphisms is quasi-finite.

Affine-space base change identifies the polynomial fibre with Spec(k[t_1,…,t_n]), for k=kappa(f(U.ι x)). Spec.stalkIso identifies R with the localization at the image prime. A polynomial ring over a field is regular, so every prime localization is regular local. Transport through the stalk ring equivalence.
